failure: A required approved/working/staged exact-byte check returned nonzero after Git text normalization. The operator incorrectly continued to commit and push. This was a publication control-flow failure, not a model or business source error.
scope: One approved payload had CRLF normalized in the first commit. The two accompanying approved notes were already byte exact. Original approval and private source evidence were not rewritten.
repair: Preserved the failed commit; added exact-path -text attributes, restaged with renormalization, reran all three approved/working/staged byte comparisons successfully, and published an additive correction.
required_future_gate: Any required raw/working/staged hash or content check returning nonzero immediately stops this publication unit. No later commit or push may run in a finally block, as an unguarded continuation, or in parallel with the failed check. Repair first, then rerun all required checks before normal publication.
limits: The incident does not change model adoption, software results, private raw evidence or runtime qualification. Successful repair does not erase the original process failure.
